deliverables.summary: Full Python signatures + docstrings for read_table, write_partition, row_count, list_ym, ym_from_filename, ym_from_date, ym_from_epoch, extract_ym_from_frame, extract_ym_from_path; four-case reader fallback contract (monolith-only, partitioned-only, mixed, empty); partition layout quote-through of architecture.md §2.4; ym truth table from §2.5; non-goals explicit (no dedup, no watermark I/O, no Postgres, no bronze, no GE, no event-time sort). T-05 acceptance criteria enumerated for developer-backend.

Per-site table (file / line / current call / target call / note) for every pd.read_parquet / rglob / ParquetFile call site. In-scope = reads under data/silver/vault/** or data/gold/marts/**. Out-of-scope sites (bronze, silver/cleaned_states, reference, tests) are enumerated so no reader escapes review. Post-PR5 enforcement grep included.

architecture_gaps_resolved: Empty-table return contract: return pd.DataFrame() (no cols), not raise FileNotFoundError. Matches current marts._read behaviour; justified against caller patterns in vault/marts.py build_* functions.

Mixed-layout precedence: partitioned wins over monolith when both are present. Not covered by architecture.md directly; derived from migration-script idempotence check (`if any(tbl.glob('ym=*')): status='already_partitioned'`).

Spark writer filename accommodation: read_table globs <ym_dir>/*.parquet (not just part.parquet) so the raw_vault_spark.py Spark emit (part-00000-*.parquet) reads transparently. Documented as reader extension in spec section 6.
Concurrent-write race: write_partition uses .part.parquet.<pid>.tmp + os.replace; last-writer-wins, no half-file visible. Defence-in-depth for future per-month-per-worker schemes.
Column pushdown is mandatory for sat_state_observation read (333M rows); spec names STATE_COLS list.

surprise_call_sites.issue: Scans silver/vault and gold/marts trees for the DE dashboard; not listed in architecture.md section 1.3 'Modules changed' table.
surprise_call_sites.recommendation: Add T-24a: migrate _scan_parquet_tree row-count to vault_io.row_count for silver_vault/gold_marts entries in PARQUET_TARGETS. Owner data-engineer, ~10 LOC, PR5.

architecture_correction_counts.marts.py_sites_reported_vs_actual: architecture said 6; actual = 9 read + 4 write = 13 entries. Over-counting is safe; checklist enumerates all.
architecture_correction_counts.raw_vault.py_sites_reported_vs_actual: architecture said 3; actual = 1 writer helper (split path) + 1 resume-count SQL swap. Bronze reads (6 sites) explicitly out of scope and flagged.
architecture_correction_counts.reconcile.py_target: architecture said 0 direct calls after switch - holds only for silver/mart counts; bronze _count_rows remains with an in-line comment.

blockers_removed_for: T-17 (postgres_sink.py staged INSERT ON CONFLICT reader path)
next_action: Dispatch T-05 (developer-backend: implement vault_io.py against vault_io_spec.md) + T-24a creation (pipeline_volumes.py migration). Spec acceptance criteria in vault_io_spec.md section 9 govern T-05 approval.

risks.description: Spec assumes pyarrow write_table preserves ym as in-file column when passed via a pandas DataFrame with ym column; regression test in T-25 verifies.
os.replace is atomic on same filesystem; cross-filesystem writes degrade to non-atomic. All current callers write under <project>/data/** which is one filesystem; documented in spec section 2.3.

Spark writer emits part-00000-*.parquet, not part.parquet; reader documented to glob *.parquet per ym dir. If a future Spark build emits a single part-00000-...parquet AND vault_io.write_partition later writes part.parquet in the same dir, concat will double-read. Mitigation: the writer for sat_state_observation Spark path explicitly deletes the ym dir before writing (idempotent overwrite); add to T-10 review.

Column pushdown for sat_state_observation drops ym from the read if STATE_COLS does not include 'ym'; add 'ym' to STATE_COLS when per-partition grouping is needed downstream (not required by current mart writer because mart filters by ym in the ym_filter itself).
